newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Koc says no short-term sale of Tofas stake.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Koc says no short-term sale of Tofas stake.

text.p: Turkey's leading industrial conglomerate Koc Holding said no sale of its stake in leading Turkish car maker Tofas to its foreign partner Fiat Spa was being considered in the "short term".

"As partners in Tofas, Koc and Fiat have held talks on investment and production plans, export development and new model plans under the competition conditions which emerged after Turkey's customs union (with the European Union)," the holding said in a statement it sent to the Istanbul Stock Exchange.
"But at this stage of the talks, there has been no development that could lead to the transfer of the shares among the partners in the short term," it added.

The Exchange had asked Koc for information after unconfirmed rumours that Fiat may buy its partner Koc's stakes in Tofas and its distributor arm Tofas Oto Ticaret sparked heavy trade in shares of Tofas, Koc and its other automotive arm Otosan on Wednesday.
Shares of Tofas gained 6.4 percent to close at 4,150 lira, Koc Holding leapt 13 percent to 15,500 and Otosan was up 11 percent to 35,500 lira yesterday.
The three shares traded at 3,750, 17,000 and 34,000 lira, respectively in morning trade on Thursday.
The Istanbul market index has surged 22.7 percent from mid-September to Wednesday's sixth consecutive all-time high close of 79,511.82, in a strong medium term uptrend.
Koc and Fiat each have 37.86 percent stake in car plant Tofas. Fiat holds a 37.5 percent stake and Koc 28.45 percent in the distributor, marketer firm Tofas Oto Ticaret.
